description: Only results classified after 12th (13th onward) are included. Results classified exactly 12th are excluded.

c.request: Looking only at back-of-the-field results, using 12 as the cutoff on classification order (`positionOrder`), and matching each result to its race: for each race (grouped by race ID and race name), show the race ID, the race name, and the average number of laps completed (`laps`, ignoring missing values). List the 10 races with the highest average first, with any race lacking an average placed last. Only results classified after 12th (13th onward) are included. Results classified exactly 12th are excluded.
c.sql:
SELECT ra.raceId AS race_id, ra.name AS race_name, AVG(CAST(res.laps AS REAL)) AS average_laps_completed
FROM results AS res
JOIN races AS ra ON ra.raceId = res.raceId
WHERE res.positionOrder > 12
  AND res.laps IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY ra.raceId, ra.name
ORDER BY average_laps_completed IS NULL, average_laps_completed DESC
LIMIT 10;

b.request: For each race, average the nonmissing `results.laps` values for drivers classified 13th or lower by race position (`positionOrder` > 12), show the race ID and name, and rank the top 10 races by average laps completed, placing races with no average last.
b.sql:
WITH race_averages AS (
  SELECT r.raceId, r.name,
         AVG(CAST(res.laps AS REAL)) AS average_laps
  FROM races AS r
  LEFT JOIN results AS res
    ON res.raceId = r.raceId
   AND res.positionOrder > 12
   AND res.laps IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY r.raceId, r.name
)
SELECT raceId, name, average_laps
FROM race_averages
ORDER BY average_laps IS NULL, average_laps DESC
LIMIT 10;
b.raw: For each race, average the nonmissing `results.laps` values for drivers classified 13th or lower by race position (`positionOrder` > 12), show the race ID and name, and rank the top 10 races by average laps completed, placing races with no average last.

d.request: Include only results with `positionOrder` greater than 12, exclude results with `positionOrder` exactly 12, and match each result to its race. Group by race ID and race name; show each race’s ID, name, and average non-missing `laps`. List 10 races ordered by average laps descending, placing races with no average last.
d.sql: SELECT races.raceId, races.name, AVG(CAST(results.laps AS REAL)) AS average_laps FROM results JOIN races ON results.raceId = races.raceId WHERE results.positionOrder > 12 AND results.positionOrder <> 12 AND results.laps IS NOT NULL GROUP BY races.raceId, races.name ORDER BY average_laps DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;

a.request: Considering only race results whose classification order (`positionOrder`) is greater than 12, each matched to its race, show for each race (grouped by race ID and race name) the race ID, the race name, and the average number of laps completed (`laps`, ignoring missing values). List the 10 races with the highest average first, with any race lacking an average placed last.
a.sql:
SELECT r.raceId, r.name AS race_name, AVG(CAST(res.laps AS REAL)) AS average_laps_completed
FROM results AS res
JOIN races AS r ON r.raceId = res.raceId
WHERE res.positionOrder > 12
  AND res.laps IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY r.raceId, r.name
ORDER BY average_laps_completed DESC
LIMIT 10;
